sandhi_exceptions.reason: Final ā before initial ṛ is left unjoined. Pāṇini allows a vowel before ṛ to stand without sandhi (optionally, there with shortening); the Purāṇic verse keeps the long ā. The metre requires the hiatus: तुष्टा ऋद्धिं प्रयच्छति has the eight syllables of the pāda, while the guṇa form तुष्टर्द्धिं would leave seven. The Gita Press prints the words apart.

sandhi.note: ā + e → ai; the final t of एतत् becomes n before the nasal m.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (also विश्वं प्रसूयते, विज्ञानं तुष्टा).
ā and ṛ stand apart; by the general rule (आद्गुणः, 6.1.87) they would fuse to ar. The hiatus keeps the pāda at eight syllables.

morph.note: Passive of the causative मोहयति ‘causes to be bewildered’: the causative -अय- is dropped before the passive -य-: मोह्-य-ते. ‘Is made deluded (by her)’. Compare 1.55, तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्.

From the divādi root सू ‘to bring forth’, which is ātmanepada (सूयते): an active verb with विश्वम् as object. Read as the passive of the adādi root (सूते, passive सूयते) it would mean ‘is born’, which does not fit the nominative सा with the accusative विश्वम्.

√याच् takes two objects (‘to ask someone for something’); in the passive participle the person asked becomes the subject (सा याचिता, ‘she, being asked’), and विज्ञानम् may be taken either as the thing asked for or as the object of प्रयच्छति. Either way she gives knowledge when asked.

mantras.anvaya: तया एतत् विश्वं मोह्यते; सा एव विश्वं प्रसूयते। सा च याचिता विज्ञानं (प्रयच्छति), तुष्टा ऋद्धिं प्रयच्छति।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two balanced pairs: a passive and an active sentence about the universe (deluded by her, brought forth by her), and two participles of condition (याचिता, तुष्टा) each with its gift, sharing the verb प्रयच्छति.
mantras.lit: By her this universe is deluded; she herself brings forth the universe. And she, when entreated, (grants) knowledge; (when) pleased, she grants prosperity.
mantras.tr: By her this universe is held in delusion, and she herself gives birth to it. Entreated, she grants knowledge; pleased, she grants prosperity.

comm.t: Medhas gathers the Goddess’s powers in four clauses: she deludes the world, she brings it forth, she gives knowledge when asked, and prosperity when pleased. The same power that binds (मोह्यते) also releases (विज्ञानम्).

The verse repeats Medhas’s first teaching in chapter 1: Mahāmāyā deludes the world (तया सम्मोह्यते जगत्, 1.55), by her the universe is emitted (तया विसृज्यते विश्वम्, 1.56), and when gracious she becomes the cause of liberation (1.57). The story has been told between the two statements.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names her as the one who deludes and the one who gives birth to the world: मोहिनी (name 562) and वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः, ‘mother of the world beginning with space’ (name 550). The parallel is of idea, not of text.

sandhi.note: Final m before t becomes anusvāra; ā + e → ai. The t of एतत् stays before the unvoiced s (खरि च, 8.4.55).

samasa.sense: the whole created universe, pictured as the cosmic egg

samasa.sense: the Goddess in her destroying form

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (its first member महामारी is a karmadhāraya: महती च असौ मारी च)
samasa.literal: she whose own form is the great Death
samasa.sense: who takes the form of the great destroyer

morph.note: वि + √आप् + क्त: i becomes y before ā (वि + आप्त → व्याप्त). ‘Reached through, pervaded’; the participle serves as the finite predicate (अस्ति understood).
Instrumental singular of the ī-stem महाकाली: -ई + -आ → -या.

mantras.anvaya: मनुजेश्वर, एतत् सकलं ब्रह्माण्डं महाकाले महामारीस्वरूपया तया महाकाल्या व्याप्तम् (अस्ति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A passive participial sentence: subject (ब्रह्माण्डम्), predicate (व्याप्तम्), agent तया expanded by महाकाल्या and its epithet; महाकाले gives the time.
mantras.lit: Pervaded by her is this entire cosmic egg, O lord of men — by Mahākālī, who at the great time (of dissolution) has the great Death (Mahāmārī) as her own form.
mantras.tr: O lord of men, this whole universe is pervaded by her — by Mahākālī, who at the great time of dissolution takes the form of Mahāmārī, the great destroyer.
mantras.tr_note: महाकाले is taken with महामारीस्वरूपया (‘at the great time, having the form of …’); it could also go with व्याप्तम् (‘at the great time the universe is pervaded by her’).

comm.t: Medhas, addressing Suratha (मनुजेश्वर), names the Goddess in her destroying aspect: Mahākālī, who at the ‘great time’ is Mahāmārī, the great Death that ends the world. In 12.8 the same word महामारी names the epidemics from which the text protects; here it is the cosmic power itself.

In the Gita Press pāṭha Mahākālī is also the presiding deity of the first carita (the liturgical viniyoga). Here the name is used in its own sense: the Goddess as Time’s destroying power at the dissolution.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also has the name Mahākālī (name 751, महाकाली). The texts remain distinct; the name is shared.

samasa.sense: the destroying power at the end of an age (as in 12.38)

morph.note: ज is the root noun from √जन् ‘born’ (as in पङ्कज, ‘mud-born’); with the negative अ-, अज/अजा is ‘unborn’. Placed beside सृष्टिः भवति, it gives the paradox: the unborn becomes creation.
Feminine of सनातन ‘everlasting’ (from सना ‘always’). The same word addresses her in the gods’ hymn, सृष्टिस्थितिविनाशानां शक्तिभूते सनातनि (11.11).

mantras.anvaya: सा एव काले महामारी (भवति); सा एव अजा सृष्टिः भवति; सा एव सनातनी काले भूतानां स्थितिं करोति।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three clauses each opened by सा एव: dissolution, creation, preservation. भवति is understood in the first.
mantras.lit: She herself at (its) time is the great Death; she herself, the unborn, becomes creation; she herself, the eternal, in time makes the continuance of beings.
mantras.tr: She alone, when the time comes, is Mahāmārī, the great destroyer; she, the unborn, becomes creation; she, the eternal, sustains all beings in their time.

comm.t: The three works of the Goddess, each introduced by सा एव, ‘she alone’: dissolution (महामारी), creation (सृष्टिः) and preservation (स्थितिः). The list begins with destruction, continuing from 12.38. The epithets underline the paradox: the unborn (अजा) becomes creation; the eternal (सनातनी) acts in time (काले).

The gods’ hymn named her the power (शक्ति) of creation, preservation and destruction (11.11), and Brahmā’s hymn said she is creation in emission and preservation in sustaining (1.76). Here Medhas states the same as plain doctrine to Suratha.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the same three functions: सृष्टिकर्त्री (name 264), गोप्त्री (name 266) and संहारिणी (name 268); it also has अजा (name 866). The shared triad is common Śākta doctrine, stated in two separate works.

morph.note: Genitive plural of the ṛ-stem नृ ‘man’: नृ + न् + आम्, with the n becoming ṇ after ṛ. (The form नॄणाम्, with long ṝ, is also taught.)
Dative of purpose: ‘for (their) destruction’. The goal of her becoming Alakṣmī is stated, not its cause.

mantras.anvaya: भवकाले सा एव नृणां गृहे वृद्धिप्रदा लक्ष्मीः (भवति)। तथा अभावे सा एव अलक्ष्मीः (भूत्वा) विनाशाय उपजायते।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two parallel sentences opposed term by term: भवकाले / अभावे, लक्ष्मीः / अलक्ष्मीः, वृद्धिप्रदा / विनाशाय.
mantras.lit: In a time of prosperity she herself is Lakṣmī in the home of men, giving increase; she herself likewise, in (a time of) decline, arises as Alakṣmī for (their) ruin.
mantras.tr: In good times she is Lakṣmī in people’s homes, bringing increase; in times of decline she herself arises as Alakṣmī, bringing ruin.

comm.t: Fortune and misfortune are both her forms. The two lines mirror each other word by word: the time of flourishing and the time of want, Lakṣmī and Alakṣmī, increase and ruin.

The gods’ hymn in chapter 4 had said the same: she is Śrī herself in the homes of the virtuous and Alakṣmī in the homes of the wicked (या श्रीः स्वयं सुकृतिनां भवनेष्वलक्ष्मीः पापात्मनाम्, 4.5). There the difference is the householder’s conduct; here it is the season of fortune.
A modern reading: the verse refuses to divide the world into a good power and a hostile one. Gain and loss come from the same source; what changes is the time.

samasa.sense: with incense, perfume and the other offerings of worship

morph.note: Present of √दा (juhotyādi): reduplicated stem ददा-. ‘She gives’ — the subject (सा, the Goddess) is carried over from 12.36–40.
Past participle of the curādi root पूज् (पूजयति): the -अय- of the present is dropped and iṭ inserted (पूजित). With सम्: ‘fully worshipped’.
Accusative plural masculine of an a-stem: -आन्. Before च it is printed पुत्रांश्च (see Sandhi).

mantras.anvaya: पुष्पैः धूपगन्धादिभिः तथा स्तुता सम्पूजिता (सा) वित्तं पुत्रान् च धर्मे मतिं शुभां गतिं (च) ददाति।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two participles of condition (स्तुता, सम्पूजिता) with instruments of worship, then the verb ददाति with four objects.
mantras.lit: Praised, and worshipped with flowers and likewise with incense, perfume and the rest, she gives wealth and sons, a mind (set) on dharma, and an auspicious course.
mantras.tr: Praised and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfume and the like, she gives wealth and children, a mind set on dharma, and a blessed destiny.
mantras.tr_note: पुत्रान्, ‘sons’, is rendered ‘children’; गतिं शुभाम्, literally ‘an auspicious going’, is rendered ‘a blessed destiny’ (the state one reaches, in this life or after it).

comm.t: The chapter of the fruits of recitation ends with a list of gifts that rises in order: wealth, children, a mind turned to dharma, and a good destiny. Praise (स्तुता) and worship (सम्पूजिता) are named together, as hymn and offering were in 12.20–24.

The closing ॐ (bīja) printed after this mantra belongs to the Gita Press pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa. The next chapter repeats the promise in Medhas’s last counsel to Suratha: worshipped, she grants enjoyment, heaven and final release (13.5).
A modern reading: the list does not stop at possessions. The last two gifts — a mind inclined to what is right, and a good end — are the ones no one can take away.
